name: Patrol pulse
goal: {{task}} One pulse is one run: it ends clean, or with new tickets in {{ticket-store}} for a human to prioritise. Nothing else changes.

template.title: Patrol pulse
template.summary: A scan lists candidate signals, a read-only investigator judges them against the project and the existing tickets, a writer files the new ones to the ticket store, and a human prioritises; one pulse is one run.
template.whenToUse: Something should be looked at on a schedule (a log, a queue, a report) and the output of each look is a triaged record for a human, never a change: run the package under the harness's scheduler and each pulse is a run.
template.notFor: Anything that should change code in the same run (use a loop with a builder), or a watch with no durable store to file into: the memory is the project's ticket file or database, named by the slot, not grooph.

slots.ask: What does this patrol watch for, in one or two sentences?
slots.example: Watch the API's log for faults users would feel: failed requests, retries that never succeed, resources running out.

slots.ask: Which command lists the candidate signals for this pulse (errors in a log, failed jobs, stale items)? It should exit non-zero when there is nothing to look at.
Which file or store holds the tickets, read by the investigator and appended to by the writer?

credits.name: u/croovies's "Lloyd" heartbeat orchestrator, as written up by explainx.ai (2026-08-14; a secondary source)
credits.note: a standing checklist per pulse, a read-only investigator, findings to a durable ticket store, humans prioritise

credits.name: Steve Yegge's Gas Town patrols
credits.note: patrol agents that loop by design; here one pulse is one run

description: A pulse, not a loop. The scan check runs the command that lists candidate signals; nothing to look at ends the pulse clean. Otherwise a read-only investigator judges each signal against the project and the tickets already filed and writes its findings; a clean verdict ends the pulse, a finding goes to a writer that owns only the ticket store, files one ticket per new finding and never files what is already filed. A human gate ends the pulse with the new tickets waiting to be prioritised. The package recurs through the harness's scheduler (the target doc says how); every pulse is its own run, so the run list is the pulse log.

check.pass: exit code 0 and at least one candidate signal printed; nothing printed is a fail and ends the pulse clean

nodes.name: Investigator
nodes.description: Read-only by policy: it may read and run, never edit. Its judgment is what separates a fault from routine noise.
nodes.brief: Judge every signal the scan listed: read the project and run what you need to tell a genuine fault from routine noise, and check {{ticket-store}} so a fault already on file is named by its ticket rather than reported as new. Write FINDINGS.md with one entry per genuine fault (the evidence, the likely cause, whether a ticket already covers it) and a line for what you dismissed and why. You investigate; you change nothing. Verdict finding when at least one genuine fault is not yet on file, clean otherwise.
outputs: FINDINGS.md: genuine faults with evidence, dismissed signals, and a verdict line

nodes.name: Ticket writer
nodes.brief: Append one ticket to {{ticket-store}} for each finding in FINDINGS.md that no existing ticket covers, in the store's own format, cross-referencing the tickets that already cover the rest. Never duplicate a ticket, never edit an existing one, and never touch code or anything outside {{ticket-store}}. Report what you filed and what you left because it was already on file in FILED.md.
outputs: {{ticket-store}} with one new ticket per new finding
FILED.md: tickets filed and findings already covered

nodes.name: Prioritise
nodes.prompt: This pulse filed new tickets in {{ticket-store}} (FILED.md says which) and changed nothing else. Prioritise them when you can; the next pulse is a new run.
